docs.title: Biola-X
docs.text:
Biola-X is Biola University Engineering's umbrella initiative for industry-connected engineering work — where students, faculty, and outside partners collaborate on real projects.

It runs across three programs:

Engineering Senior Capstone Summer Engineering Internships Industry Partnerships

docs.title: The three programs
docs.text:
• Engineering Senior Capstone

    Year-long, team-based senior design projects sponsored by industry and community partners. This section holds the live catalog of project ideas for the upcoming year and the proposal form for new sponsors.

  • Summer Engineering Internships (SEI)

    Paid summer research and development placements where students tackle a focused engineering problem over 8–10 weeks. This section documents completed SEI projects.

  • Industry Partnerships

    Ongoing relationships with companies and agencies that sponsor projects, host interns, mentor teams, and hire graduates. This section tracks each partner organization and the state of the engagement.

docs.title: Engineering Senior Capstone
docs.text:
Part of the Biola-X initiative.

A living catalog of project ideas for Biola University's 2026–27 Engineering Senior Capstone. Each idea is tracked with its sponsor, scholarship / funding, and expected deliverables, and is updated as the concept evolves.

Rather than filling out the proposal form separately for every idea, the form points here — reviewers and potential sponsors can browse everything in one place.

docs.title: 01 · Autonomous Campus Delivery Cart
docs.text:
Exploring Last updated: 2026-08-29

Example idea

This is placeholder content to show the format. Replace it with a real idea or delete the file.

  • Capstone Project Idea

    A small (roughly golf-cart-sized or smaller) electric vehicle that can autonomously carry mail, lab supplies, and packages between buildings on the La Mirada campus along a fixed set of paved routes. Core challenges: low-speed obstacle detection and pedestrian safety, GPS + wheel-odometry localization under tree cover, a simple web interface for requesting a pickup, and a fail-safe manual override.

  • Sponsor

    Potential: Biola Facilities Services / Mail Center. Contact: TBD. Willing to act as project client and meet 1–2×/month: Maybe — need more information. Prototype ownership: Facilities would keep the cart for continued campus use.

  • Scholarship

    Estimated budget $4,000–$7,000 (used electric base vehicle, compute, sensors, safety hardware). Funding source under discussion — possible split between Facilities and the Engineering department materials budget. No named student scholarship attached yet.

  • Deliverables

    • Operational prototype cart with autonomous navigation on 2–3 mapped routes
    • Safety case document and test results (stopping distance, obstacle response)
    • Pickup-request web app and operator dashboard
    • Full CAD, wiring diagrams, and source code repository
    • Final report and Senior Design Showcase presentation

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Confirm campus rules on autonomous vehicles on walkways with Campus Safety.
  • Ask Facilities for current daily delivery volume and routes.

docs.title: 02 · Low-Cost Water Quality Sensor Buoy
docs.text:
Draft Last updated: 2026-08-29

Example idea

This is placeholder content to show the format. Replace it with a real idea or delete the file.

  • Capstone Project Idea

    A solar-powered floating buoy that continuously logs water temperature, pH, turbidity, and dissolved oxygen for a local watershed or coastal partner, and uploads readings over cellular to a public dashboard. Target build cost well under commercial equivalents. Challenges: waterproofing and biofouling, power budgeting for year-round operation, sensor calibration and drift, and mooring design.

  • Sponsor

    Potential: a regional water district, watershed conservancy, or Biola Biology department. Contact: TBD. Client meetings 1–2×/month: TBD. Prototype ownership: sponsor keeps the deployed buoy and data.

  • Scholarship

    Estimated materials budget $1,500–$3,000 per buoy. Possible funding via a sponsor grant or environmental education fund. Open to a small stipend for field-deployment work.

  • Deliverables

    • One deployed, weatherized buoy with 4-parameter sensing
    • Cloud dashboard with historical charts and CSV export
    • Calibration procedure and maintenance guide
    • Bill of materials and assembly instructions for replication
    • Final report and showcase presentation

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Identify a partner with an accessible, permitted deployment site.
  • Check whether existing monitoring data exists for comparison / validation.

docs.title: 03 · Adaptive Controller for Accessible Gaming
docs.text:
Draft Last updated: 2026-08-29

Example idea

This is placeholder content to show the format. Replace it with a real idea or delete the file.

  • Capstone Project Idea

    A configurable, low-cost input device that lets gamers with limited hand mobility remap buttons and joystick axes to large external switches, foot pedals, or sip-and-puff inputs. Presents to a PC or console as a standard controller. Challenges: ergonomics for a specific user, latency, a friendly remapping app, and a 3D-printable modular enclosure.

  • Sponsor

    Potential: a local occupational therapy clinic, an accessibility nonprofit, or an individual end user identified with a partner org. Contact: TBD. Client meetings 1–2×/month: TBD. Prototype ownership: the end user keeps the finished device.

  • Scholarship

    Estimated materials budget $600–$1,200. Low enough to fund from the Engineering department materials budget if no external sponsor is secured.

  • Deliverables

    • Working adaptive controller fitted to one real user's needs
    • Remapping/configuration desktop app
    • 3D print files and assembly guide for the modular enclosure
    • Firmware source repository
    • User testing results, final report, and showcase presentation

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Recruit an end user early; the design must be driven by their specific needs.
  • Review Microsoft's Xbox Adaptive Controller jack standard (3.5 mm) for compatibility with existing accessible switches.

docs.title: Industry Partnerships

A partner might sponsor a capstone team, host a summer intern, mentor students, provide equipment, or hire graduates — often several of these over time. docs.title: Summer Engineering Internships (SEI)
docs.text:
Part of the Biola-X initiative.

The Summer Engineering Internship program places one or two students on a focused engineering problem for 8–10 weeks over the summer, working with a faculty advisor and — where there is one — an industry or community partner. Each internship ends with a working deliverable and a short technical report.

This page is an archive of completed SEI projects.

Placeholder content

The projects below are placeholders showing the format. Replace the details (year, students, partner, outcomes) with the real records, or remove the ones that do not apply.

Status key

Completed finished and documented  ·  In progress currently running  ·  On hold paused or seeking funding

docs.title: Completed projects
docs.text:
• Formula-Style Car Suspension Redesign

    Completed 2024

    Redesigned the front suspension geometry and uprights for the student formula vehicle to reduce unsprung mass and improve camber control.

    • Partner: [internal — Motorsports team]
    • Deliverable: CAD package, FEA report, fabricated prototype uprights

  • Zebrafish Behavioral Assay Rig

    Completed 2024

    Built an automated imaging and stimulus rig for zebrafish larvae, with tracking software to quantify startle response for a biology research lab.

    • Partner: [Biola Biology Department]
    • Deliverable: Enclosure + camera rig, tracking pipeline, calibration guide

  • Lunar Surface Navigation Algorithm

    Completed 2023

    Developed and simulated a terrain-relative navigation approach for a small lunar rover using crater-matching against orbital imagery.

    • Partner: [Aerospace partner — TBD]
    • Deliverable: Simulation code, accuracy analysis, conference-style paper

  • UAV Payload Release Mechanism

    Completed 2023

    Designed a lightweight servo-actuated release for a fixed-wing UAV to drop small sensor packages at GPS waypoints.

    • Partner: [Defense / robotics partner — TBD]
    • Deliverable: Mechanism, flight-test data, integration documentation

  • Cable-Driven Prosthetic Hand

    Completed 2022

    Prototyped a 3D-printed, tendon-actuated prosthetic hand with a myoelectric input, targeting a low parts cost for humanitarian distribution.

    • Partner: [Nonprofit partner — TBD]
    • Deliverable: Working hand, print files, assembly and fitting manual

  • Municipal Water Quality Telemetry

    Completed 2022

    Instrumented a partner water district's sample sites with cellular data loggers and a dashboard for pH, turbidity, and conductivity.

    • Partner: [Regional water district — TBD]
    • Deliverable: Logger units, cloud dashboard, maintenance runbook

  • Off-Grid Clinic Solar Microgrid Controller

    Completed 2021

    Built a charge / load controller and monitoring system for a small solar installation at a rural clinic, with remote fault alerts.

    • Partner: [Medical missions partner — TBD]
    • Deliverable: Controller hardware, firmware, commissioning report

  • Additively-Manufactured Heat Exchanger

    Completed 2021

    Designed and tested a compact metal-printed heat exchanger with internal lattice channels, benchmarked against a conventional plate design.

    • Partner: [Manufacturing partner — TBD]
    • Deliverable: Printed prototypes, thermal test data, design guidelines

docs.title: Add a completed project
docs.text:
1. Copy one of the - card blocks above.
  2. Update the icon, title, status pill (completed / active / paused), summary, partner, and deliverable.
  3. Keep the cards in reverse-chronological order (newest first).
  4. Commit and push — the site rebuilds automatically.

For a longer write-up, create a file at docs/sei/<project-slug>.md, link the card title to it, and add a nav line under Summer Engineering Internships in mkdocs.yml.
